After 2 years in the Roivant rotational analyst program, I'm thrilled to share that I've found a home at Immunovant . After supporting Immunovant in a clinical development / data analytics capacity, I'm excited to officially join the team as a Senior Analyst, Data Infrastructure/AI. Immunovant is developing targeted therapies for autoimmune diseases, including a potential new treatment for Graves' disease, where the standard of care hasn't changed in over 70 years. I'm looking forward to continuing to support our Graves' disease program and scale our data approach across the portfolio.

TL;DR - graduated from Duke in May, moving to SF, and now writing about energy and what comes next on Substack ( https://lnkd.in/gzEEYRV3 ). More on Duke and all the things I'm grateful for below! Collaborating with and learning from Bryan Koen over the past four years helped me find my passion for energy, but more importantly changed how I approach problems and think about the world. I'm so grateful to Bryan, Stacy Peterson, M.Ed. , Brian Murray , Chris Wedding , Judy Ledlee, Ph.D., P.E. , Rich Herbst , Carl Thompson , Colleen Nieto and everyone else at the Nicholas Institute for Energy, Environment & Sustainability + Duke's energy/climate community for the time, dedication, and genuine care they've shown for me and all of their students. Without a doubt, the highlight of my time at Duke was working with Mudit Agrawal , Margaret Berei , Daniel Ketyer , and our amazing team to build Energy and Climate Ventures at Duke from a single course into a full-fledged program. The alumni and students we've met along the way are an inspiration, and I can't wait to see what this community becomes. The Duke Energy and Climate Club was my home on campus, and leading an incredible team with Nicholas Nease this past year has me so excited for the future of energy at Duke. Similarly, working with Chloe Young at Energy Terminal has led to friendships I otherwise never would have made - for any current students, make sure to join! And while I could go another four years without planning another event, running Duke Energy Week with Madeleine Fox will always be a high point. Although I didn't have the easiest time in econometrics, exploring community opposition to solar development in my senior thesis under Jeffrey DeSimone was a wonderful experience, and one I never thought I'd have when I declared economics. I also didn't expect to participate in any kind of group research - big thank you to Tom J. Cinq-Mars for teaching the class that got me hooked on energy, and for supporting our data center design capstone with the original FOCUS crew, Aaron Siegle , Parker Peverley , and Matthew Koh Jia An . Perhaps my only non-energy Duke project was helping Steve Columbaro build and offer a brand-new course, MMS 390: Business Fundamentals, for students like me interested in business and trying to figure out what that means - thank you to Steve for being an incredible resource to me and so many other students over the years. Finally, thank you to everyone who put up with me at various internships throughout Duke - I've learned so much from you and will always be grateful for your time and mentorship - Ryan Rutledge , Zoe Draghi , Rachel Fricke and John Pressley , Sean Pavel , Stephanie Simon , Luke Del Core , and Jack Sloan . More updates soon, but until then, I'll be writing about energy news, innovation, and other interest areas on my new Substack - feel free to give it a look if that's interesting to you. And for anyone in SF/Bay Area, please reach out - would love to catch up!

In May, I graduated from Duke University as a Karsh International Merit Scholar, with a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and Sociology (with distinction) and a certificate in Child Policy Research. At Duke, I fell in love with the social sciences, found friends who've become family, and met faculty mentors who continually inspire me. These have been truly life-changing four years. This fall, I will be starting my M.Phil. at the University of Oxford , as a Department of Sociology, University of Oxford scholar and a member of Kellogg College. I am excited to continue working on family sociology and welfare policy evaluation, as well as bridging these interests with formal demographic modelling and advanced quantitative methods. Going from one dream university to another, I could not be more grateful. Stoked for this next chapter, but as always, #GoDuke 💙 😈

After a few years of learning by building Styl AI and at Sage AI Labs , I’m excited to share that I’ve joined Whop as a Software Engineer on the Core Product team in Palo Alto. It feels fitting that my first job after university is at a company built around people taking unconventional paths and creating businesses of their own. I’ve always been drawn to the intersection of technology, entrepreneurship, and the internet, and Whop is tackling some of the most interesting problems in this space. What has stood out most, though, is the people. The team is incredibly sharp, ambitious, and welcoming. Even in my first two weeks, I’ve learned a tremendous amount from everyone around me, and I’m excited for what’s ahead. Grateful for the opportunity and looking forward to building. 🚀

Today, Kikoff is excited to announce the acquisition of The Service Bureau's technology, customer relationships, and team. Since day one, Kikoff's mission has been to empower everyone to achieve financial security. As we've grown, we've expanded that mission beyond helping consumers directly to strengthening the infrastructure that powers the entire credit ecosystem. Bringing TSB technology into Kikoff is an important step in that journey. For more than three decades, TSB has built a best-in-class reputation for reliable, compliant credit reporting infrastructure. We're honored to build on that legacy as we continue expanding Kikoff Enterprise and giving more organizations the tools they need to better serve their communities.
